title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Environmental Science (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Environmental Science (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: EIA is usually required for a development project when
options: Limited impacts are expected in the environment
small area is expected to be affected by the project
There are potentials for trans-boundary impact
questions.explanation: EIA is required when there are potentials for trans-boundary impacts.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is inclusive or holistic to the other?
questions.explanation: Species diversity encompasses species richness, evenness, and relative commonness.

questions.questionText: Why is biodiversity rich in tropics?
options: Have low suitable environment that temperate
Tropic communities have more specialization for adaptation
Temperate communities are older than tropic community
questions.explanation: Tropic communities have more specialization for adaptation, leading to higher biodiversity.

questions.questionText: Waste audit means that
options: The amount of waste created in the production process is checked
An assessment of how much solid waste product will generate is performed
An assessment of how much unnecessary waste a product will generate when its life cycle is to be completed is estimated
questions.explanation: A waste audit assesses unnecessary waste generated throughout a product's life cycle.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is not the basic element for secondary biological treatment?
options: Contact between the organic material and the microbe
questions.explanation: Different chemicals are not a basic element for secondary biological treatment.

questions.questionText: From the different kinds of pollutants which are non-biodegradable and persist in the environment for a prolonged time?
questions.explanation: Synthetic pollutants are non-biodegradable and persist in the environment.

questions.questionText: Of the following which one is false about in situ and ex situ conservation?
options: In-situ conservation is more dynamic, whereas ex-situ conservation is more static/fixed.
In-situ conservation is time-consuming but more sustainable while ex-situ conservation methods are aimed to use in conserving genetic components, in immediate occasions.
In-situ conservation is done in the natural habitats of the biodiversity components while ex-situ conservation is done outside of their natural habitats.
In Ex-situ conservation, populations remain within the ecosystem involving the process of evolution whereas, in in-situ conservation, they are not involving the natural evolution process.
questions.explanation: In ex-situ conservation, populations do not remain within their ecosystem.

questions.questionText: What is an intangible benefit of ISO 14000?
questions.explanation: Improved community goodwill is an intangible benefit of ISO 14000.

questions.questionText: Today the world faces two urgent and interconnected challenges related to modern energy services based on where they are available and not; the key Solution to both challenges are:
options: Provide sustainable energy for all – energy that is accessible, cleaner and more efficient.
Provide renewable energy and energy efficient for all.
questions.explanation: Both A and C focus on sustainable and efficient energy solutions.

questions.questionText: During biodiversity assessment
options: No matter about the representative of the ecosystem/site as a whole.
All species groups to be compared through time and between sites should be sampled in exactly in different way.
The delimitation of the ecosystem/site to be sampled needs to be clarified before sampling.
No need of scaling distances between sub-sample sites.
questions.explanation: Clarifying the delimitation of the ecosystem/site is essential before sampling.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the 'screening' step of EIA?
options: To assess the quality of the project design
To facilitate informed decision making by providing clear, well-structured, factual analysis of the effects and consequences of proposed actions
To determine whether a full EIA is needed
To give decisions on draft EIA report
questions.explanation: The screening step determines if a full EIA is necessary.

questions.questionText: Which of the following drainage pattern is characterized by tributaries flowing in the same direction as the main stream and joins at acute angle?
questions.explanation: Dendritic drainage patterns have tributaries joining the main stream at acute angles in a tree-like pattern, resembling branches on a tree.

questions.questionText: _____ Devices remove materials which would damage equipment or interfere with a process.
questions.explanation: Screening devices are used to remove harmful materials.

questions.questionText: In some mini watersheds of Somali region, the land is characterized by shallow, dry soil, not too steep, and available stones; such dry zones which measure with water harvesting effect for effective tree planting purposes should be implemented
questions.explanation: Bench terraces are effective for tree planting in such conditions.

questions.questionText: The primary reason for Environmental Impact Assessment is to;
options: Mitigate existing environmental impacts of development
Predict the size of impacts of developments
Identify the environmental consequences of development in advance
questions.explanation: EIA aims to identify potential environmental consequences before development.

questions.questionText: What does the ISO - 14000 cover?
questions.explanation: ISO 14000 encompasses all listed aspects of environmental management.

questions.questionText: Suppose environmentalists incorporate pollution controls, based on studies of anticipated environmental effects at the initial planning stage to identify, predict and evaluate the potential environmental effects of a proposed project. What types of environmental pollution control measures are carried out by the Environmentalists?
questions.explanation: Environmental pollution assessments are crucial for evaluating potential effects.

questions.questionText: Which of the ISO 14000 series of standards focuses on life cycle assessment?
questions.explanation: ISO 14040 focuses on life cycle assessment.

questions.questionText: Why is the sludge aerated?
questions.explanation: Aeration increases bacterial growth, which is essential for treatment.

questions.questionText: A Solar cell is an electrical device that converts the energy of light directly into electricity by the _____________
questions.explanation: Solar cells operate based on the photovoltaic effect.

questions.questionText: How does ISO 14001 define an 'environmental impact'?
options: Change to the environment, whether adverse or beneficial, wholly or partially resulting from an organisation's environmental aspects
An adverse change to the environment, wholly or partially resulting from an organisation's environmental aspects
negative environmental change, wholly resulting from an organisation's environmental aspects
Change to the environment caused directly, or indirectly by an organisation
questions.explanation: ISO 14001 defines environmental impact as any change resulting from an organization's activities.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true about guiding principles of Environmental Education?
options: It is interdisciplinary in its approach
It implicitly considers environmental aspects of plan for development and growth
It is a continuous life-saving process
It considers the environment in its totality, natural and built technological and social structures
questions.explanation: Environmental education is a continuous lifelong process, not primarily a 'life-saving' process. It focuses on developing knowledge, awareness, and skills throughout one's life.

questions.questionText: How many organizations/companies worldwide have certified environmental management systems?
questions.explanation: According to ISO survey data, between 10,000 and 100,000 organizations worldwide have certified environmental management systems (this number has actually grown to over 300,000 in recent years).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following are the correct examples of non-renewable resources that cannot replenish?
questions.explanation: Petrol, coal, and gas are non-renewable resources.

questions.questionText: What is the growth of huge amounts of algae and other aquatic plants leading to the deterioration of the water quality called?
questions.explanation: Eutrophication refers to the excessive growth of algae due to nutrient overload.

questions.questionText: Which one is NOT the Source of errors during sampling?
questions.explanation: Sample homogeneity is not a source of error but rather a characteristic of the sample.

questions.questionText: Among the following level of biological organization, which one is relatively practicable for toxicity testing?
questions.explanation: Testing at the organism level is practical for toxicity assessments.

questions.questionText: Who is responsible for reviewing the organization's environmental management system at planned intervals?
questions.explanation: Top management is responsible for reviewing the environmental management system.

questions.questionText: Which of the following EIA processes comes first?
questions.explanation: Impact identifying is the first step in the EIA process.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a step during Delineating watershed from topographic map?
options: Locating the river, lake, stream, wetland, or other water bodies of interest, then circling at the outlet or downstream point

Marking at the high points along both sides of the watercourse, working your way upstream towards the headwaters of the watershed, then drawing a line connecting the 'marked points' along one side of the watercourse
Flow directions created using flow direction and accumulation tool in Arc SWAT
Containing the line until it passes around the head of the watershed and down the opposite side of the watercourse, eventually connecting with the circle started with
questions.explanation: Flow directions are not a step in delineating a watershed from a topographic map.

questions.questionText: Which one is ancient and widely used technology that removes particles and at least some microbes from the water?
questions.explanation: The sedimentation process is an ancient method for water purification.

questions.questionText: Which of the ISO 14000 series of standards focuses on environmental auditing?
questions.explanation: ISO 14010 (along with 14011 and 14012, now consolidated under 14001) established guidelines for environmental auditing principles and procedures.

questions.questionText: The feature of environmental education that helps social groups and individuals gain a variety of experience in and acquire a basic understanding of the environment and its associated problems is?
questions.explanation: Knowledge is a core feature of environmental education.

questions.questionText: Bhopal Gas Disaster is a kind of
questions.explanation: The Bhopal Gas Disaster is classified as a manmade disaster.

questions.questionText: Community Gene Bank has the following significances except?
options: Provide full information about these resources
Broaden farmers' options regarding variety choice
questions.explanation: Neglecting diversity conservation is not a significance of Community Gene Banks.

questions.questionText: Among Collection or Conveyance Systems of wastewater which one collects commercial and household wastes and sometimes industrial wastes?
questions.explanation: Combined sewers collect both commercial and household wastes.

questions.questionText: What is the most common coagulant used during chemical treatment?
questions.explanation: Alum is the most commonly used coagulant in water treatment.

questions.questionText: Disadvantage of in situ conservation
options: It is easy to control illegal exploitation
The environment may need restoring and alien species are difficult to control
It needs high cost that ex situ conservation
questions.explanation: In situ conservation can face challenges with alien species and environmental restoration.

questions.questionText: Suppose environmental education in formal and adult education programmes needs to be supported by the media. The print media like newspapers and magazines is one alternative for literate population. Which one of the following is not true according to the above idea?
options: Acquaint with the conservation needs, problems and efforts
Enable exposure to real life situations
Oblivious with the philosophy and practice of sustainable development
questions.explanation: The media should not be oblivious to sustainable development practices.

questions.questionText: Suppose the invisible water vapor gets bigger and forms visible liquid water and falling/reaching the ground as rain and snow. These two processes respectively known as…..
questions.explanation: Condensation forms liquid water, which then falls as precipitation.

questions.questionText: According to climate science, which of the following parameters does not contribute to the cause of climate forcing?
questions.explanation: Constant insolation and sunlight do not contribute to climate forcing.

questions.questionText: Which one is the key and primary focus area of mitigation measures in EIA?
options: The identification of compensation mechanisms for those impacts that are unavoidable and cannot be reduced further
Measures that focus on limiting or lessening the severity and the duration of the impacts
Preventive measures that avoid the occurrence of impacts and thus avoid harm or even produce positive outcomes.
Works on the monetary compensation for displaced communities
questions.explanation: Preventive measures are the primary focus of mitigation in EIA.

questions.questionText: Which natural causes of climate change results in the movement of warm water from the equator back towards the poles and deep ocean circulation of cold water from the poles towards the equator?
questions.explanation: Ocean currents are responsible for the movement of warm and cold water.

questions.questionText: Of the following one is false about biodiversity?
options: Biodiversity also includes genetic differences within each species
Biodiversity contributes to our material well-being
Biodiversity is similarity of life in all its forms and at all levels of organization
Biodiversity conservation contributes for environmental well-being
questions.explanation: Biodiversity encompasses variety, not similarity.

questions.questionText: Day time noise standard prescribed for residential areas is
questions.explanation: The daytime noise standard for residential areas is typically set at 55dB according to WHO guidelines and many national environmental standards.

questions.questionText: Which one is false about the distribution of biodiversity across the globe?
options: Geography and the presence of other species affect biodiversity distribution.
Generally, diversity consistently measures higher in the tropics and lower in polar regions.
Biodiversity is consistently distributed; rather it varies greatly across the globe as well as within regions.
Biodiversity is not evenly distributed; rather it varies greatly across the globe as well as within regions.
questions.explanation: Biodiversity is not consistently distributed; it varies significantly.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a benefit of implementing ISO 14001?
options: Automatic compliance with all applicable regulations
questions.explanation: ISO 14001 does not guarantee automatic compliance with regulations.

questions.questionText: A manufacturing company is audited by a third-party certification body as part of their EMS certification. The auditor identifies a number of areas where the company is not meeting the required standard. What terminology is used to describe these areas?
questions.explanation: Areas not meeting standards are referred to as nonconformities.

questions.questionText: Organizations are required to comply with legal requirements related to an organization's environmental aspects. If applicable, these can include:
options: International, national and local laws and regulations
Rules or guidance from regulatory agencies
Requirements from government entities or other relevant authorities
questions.explanation: All listed options are legal requirements for organizations.

questions.questionText: Assume you are an advisor to one Manufacturing Company with environmental aspects, which of the following is not possible advice you may give as an environmentalist?
options: The company to develop manufacturing processes with minimum environmental impact, particularly the production
The company to educate, train, and motivate their employees
The company to maximize the recyclability of waste components
The company as adopting environmental management system to the organization is too costly
questions.explanation: Advising against adopting an EMS due to cost is not a valid recommendation.

questions.questionText: EIA is necessary because …………
options: Development is bad for the environment
There is growing interest in sustainability
Environmental impacts of developments are of public interest
questions.explanation: EIA is necessary to address public interest in environmental impacts.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an external climate forcing mechanism of the Earth system?
options: Earth's orbital variation around the Sun
The changing composition of the atmosphere
Volcanic pollution and dust and aerosol
questions.explanation: Earth's orbital variations are external climate forcing mechanisms.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT a strategic goal of Energy Reduction techniques?
options: To reduce CO2 emissions and local environmental impacts
To improve economic productivity and promote industry development
To improve economic resilience and reduce energy deprivation
To provide non-renewable energy for all
questions.explanation: Providing non-renewable energy is not a goal of energy reduction techniques.

questions.questionText: Among the following ……………………………..is the political and ethical movement that seeks to improve and protect the quality of the natural environment through changes to environmentally harmful human activities.
questions.explanation: Environmentalism is the movement focused on protecting the environment.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not attributed to drinking water?
questions.explanation: Source is not an attribute of drinking water quality.

questions.questionText: Which is the most common treatment process in potable or drinking water treatment?
options: Chemical and biological water treatment process
Biological and physical water treatment process
Physical and chemical water treatment process
Physical and biological water treatment process
questions.explanation: The most common treatment process involves both physical and chemical methods.

questions.questionText: Which type of pollutant is released into the environment from diffuse and multiple causes and is often difficult to trace back to its origin and has a range of negative impacts on the environment?
questions.explanation: Non-point source pollutants are difficult to trace and have widespread impacts.

questions.questionText: Which one is FALSE regarding Collecting soil samples for the test?
options: Remove all grass and rocks from the testing area
Label each sample jar or bag with your name, the collection date, and what you want to be tested
Keep samples in a cool, dry place until they can be delivered to the lab.
Soil samples be taken from single locations
questions.explanation: Soil samples should be taken from multiple locations for accuracy.

questions.questionText: Climate is differing from weather in that, Climate is;
options: It is a condition of the atmosphere at any particular time and place
It is the occurrence of a dominant weather element over an area for an extended period of time
It is a visible mass of tiny water droplets and/or ice crystals that are above the earth's surface
It is the accumulation of daily and seasonal weather events for a certain period of time.
questions.explanation: Climate refers to the long-term pattern of weather in a particular area, typically averaged over 30 years. It's the accumulation of daily and seasonal weather events over time, not just dominant weather elements.

questions.questionText: Which region has been the primary contributor to CO2 emissions?
questions.explanation: The Global North has historically contributed the most to CO2 emissions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following does not help in disinfecting water?
questions.explanation: Filtration does not disinfect but removes particles.

questions.questionText: Which is the measure of light-transmitting properties of water and is comprised of suspended and colloidal material?
questions.explanation: Turbidity measures the clarity of water based on suspended particles.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is INCORRECT about Sustainable Energy?
options: It's a form of energy that meets our today's demand of energy without putting them in danger of getting expired and can be used over and over again.
It can cause harm to the environment and Human Health
Its sources of energy can best be used to power homes and industries without any harmful effects being experienced.
Its energy that is accessible, cleaner and more efficient.
questions.explanation: Sustainable energy should not cause harm to the environment.

questions.questionText: When the sewage becomes stronger, the turbidity of wastewater?
questions.explanation: Stronger sewage typically increases turbidity due to higher solids content.

questions.questionText: The maximum ozone layer has been observed in which of the following?
questions.explanation: The maximum concentration of the ozone layer is found in the mid-latitude temperate regions. While ozone depletion (ozone hole) is observed over the Antarctic (south pole), this doesn't mean maximum ozone is located there.

questions.questionText: ……………………………………………………………… is a multi-dimensional process that involves major changes in social structures, attitudes, and institutions, as well as economic growth, reduction of inequality, and eradication of absolute poverty.
questions.explanation: Sustainable development encompasses social, economic, and environmental changes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not termed as the technical heart of environmental impact analysis during the EIA process?
questions.explanation: Impact mitigation is not considered the technical heart of EIA.

questions.questionText: Cyclones occurring in the North Atlantic ocean are called
questions.explanation: Cyclones in the North Atlantic are referred to as hurricanes.

questions.questionText: ___ is a long-term maintenance of ecosystem biodiversity through the management of multiple forms of resource use.
questions.explanation: Conservation involves managing resources to maintain biodiversity.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statement is true about the concept of Environmental Education?
options: Enables learners to develop a structure of knowledge about the environment and world
Hinders learners by enabling them to participate in a sustainable future
Delays awareness, concern and knowledge about the environment
Impede understanding to preserve and utilize the environment in a sustainable manner for the benefit of future generations
questions.explanation: Environmental education aims to enhance knowledge and awareness.

questions.questionText: A core part of Impact Management is developing an EMP (environmental management plan). Which items from the list below are not contents of the EMP?
questions.explanation: TOR (Terms of Reference) is not typically a content of the EMP.

questions.questionText: What is Ring of Fire?
options: Belt of volcanoes in the Circum Pacific region
Belt of volcanoes in the mid-continental region
Belt of volcanoes in the mid-Atlantic region
questions.explanation: The Ring of Fire is a major area in the basin of the Pacific Ocean where approximately 75% of the world's active volcanoes are located and about 90% of the world's earthquakes occur due to tectonic plate movements.

questions.questionText: A petroleum refinery plant discharges toxic chemicals into a river at an unknown period. If you want to site assessment for the identification of the contaminated source, which one of the following sampling techniques is likely the best favorable?
questions.explanation: Judgmental sampling is often used in site assessments to target specific areas of concern.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a requirement of the 'performance evaluation' in ISO 14001?
questions.explanation: Identifying improvement opportunities is a key requirement in performance evaluation.

questions.questionText: An activated sludge system consists of two components, an aerator and ________
questions.explanation: An activated sludge system typically includes a clarifier.

questions.questionText: Climate warming can affect species in the following principal ways except?
options: Alterations of species densities (including altered community composition and structure)
Range shifts, either poleward or upward in elevation
Changes in morphology, such as body size
Increment in genetic diversity that leads to inbreeding depression.
questions.explanation: Climate warming typically does not lead to increased genetic diversity.

questions.questionText: ISO – 14001 gives stress on
questions.explanation: ISO 14001 emphasizes the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle for environmental management.

questions.questionText: A disease that becomes unusually widespread and even global in its reach is referred to as
questions.explanation: A pandemic is a disease that spreads across a large region, affecting a significant portion of the population.

questions.questionText: ……………… is stumbling of the rock out of its original position.
questions.explanation: Falls refer to the sudden, free-falling movement of rocks or soil masses detaching from steep slopes or cliffs, moving downward primarily through the air.

questions.questionText: What is the most toxic organ in the body?
questions.explanation: The liver is often considered the most toxic organ due to its role in detoxification.

questions.questionText: Assume gases, liquids, and dissolved solids are concentrated on the solid surface. It may also adhere to a surface of liquid as the result of surface or chemical force. The form of gaseous pollutant control device applied is probably?
questions.explanation: Adsorption is the process where pollutants adhere to solid surfaces.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following does not include in an Impact assessment?
options: detailed assessment of the planned project and selected alternatives compared to the baseline conditions
Qualitative descriptions measuring high, medium and low impacts
Quantitative descriptions such as indicating the cubic meters of water withdrawn, sewage produced, and pollutants released
All the data collection, analyses, and developed plans summarized together in a well-structured and concise document
questions.explanation: Impact assessments do not typically summarize all data in a single document.

questions.questionText: Which one is not true of the Scoping step?
options: It is a systematic exercise that establishes the boundaries of an EIA
It clearly indicates what is relevant and what is not relevant within an EIA
It serves as a work plan for the entire EIA process
It indicates methodological approach for impact analysis
questions.explanation: The scoping step does not typically indicate the methodological approach.

questions.questionText: What is the role of top management in ISO 14001?
options: To delegate environmental management responsibilities to middle managers
To establish policies and objectives for the environmental management system
To perform all internal audits of the environmental management system
To determine the training requirements for all employees
questions.explanation: Top management is responsible for establishing policies and objectives.

questions.questionText: It is believed that women play an important role in watershed management because of the following ideas/truths except
options: Women are highly dependent on the environment
Watershed degradation impact is more on women.
It is the Women's who degrade the watershed, so should take more responsibility
questions.explanation: The statement blaming women for watershed degradation is not accurate.

questions.questionText: The point of the earth's surface directly above the point where an earthquake occurs is called the:
questions.explanation: The epicenter is the point directly above the earthquake's focus.

questions.questionText: The extent to which a community, structure, services or geographic area is likely to be damaged or disrupted by the impact of a particular hazard is termed as
questions.explanation: Vulnerability refers to the susceptibility to damage from hazards.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a requirement of the 'Emergency preparedness and response' in ISO 14001?
options: Identifying and evaluating environmental aspects and impacts
Establishing and maintaining procedures for response to environmental emergencies
questions.explanation: Establishing emergency response procedures is a key requirement.

questions.questionText: Which form of energy is currently causing the largest amount of greenhouse gas emissions, globally?
questions.explanation: Coal is the largest contributor to global greenhouse gas emissions.

questions.questionText: Which ISO sits within the ISO 14000 family of standards is internationally recognized EMS standard which provides organizations with a framework to protect the environment, and respond to changing environmental conditions in balance with socio-economic needs?
questions.explanation: ISO 14001 is the recognized standard for environmental management systems.

questions.questionText: Short-term tests designed to measure the effects of toxic agents on aquatic species during a short period of their life span is
questions.explanation: Acute toxicity tests measure short-term effects of toxins.

questions.questionText: Of the following which one are advantages of in situ conservation?
options: The species will continue to evolve in their environment
It is expensive to keep an organism in its natural habitat
Small breeding populations can be kept
questions.explanation: In situ conservation allows species to evolve naturally in their habitats.

questions.questionText: Why Biodiversity Assessment/Measurement?
options: To avoid priority setting and identifying conservation strategies
To know distribution patterns of species and habitat
To misunderstand the status of our biodiversity resources
To increase negative impacts on the environment
questions.explanation: Biodiversity assessment helps understand species distribution and habitat status.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the physical characteristics of water?
questions.explanation: Turbidity measures the physical clarity of water.

questions.questionText: Which one of these electric generating plants is most responsible for global warming?
questions.explanation: Coal-fueled plants are significant contributors to global warming.

questions.questionText: One of the following is a method of assigning a numeric order to links in a stream network.
questions.explanation: Stream order is a method for classifying streams based on their position in the network.

questions.questionText: One of the following EIA data collection tools provides quantitative estimates of impact magnitude and significance?
questions.explanation: Complex matrices provide detailed quantitative assessments in EIA.

questions.questionText: Criteria which is NOT important in developing a sampling design?
options: Where are samples to be collected?
When are samples to be collected?
How many samples are to be collected?
questions.explanation: Stating the sample problem is not a criterion for sampling design.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following energy resources produces radioactive waste?
questions.explanation: Nuclear energy production generates radioactive waste.

questions.questionText: The Arsi-Bale massive and northern part of Ethiopia is known for steep slopes and there is farming on extremely steep hillsides causing watershed degradation. Which method is the best for management of watersheds and control the runoff of water in such areas?
questions.explanation: Terracing is effective for managing steep slopes and controlling runoff.
